content.text: I found that FeVO4 (mp-504509) sits on the hull, so its region is my first target. Next I'm measuring index 76 (Fe≈V, low Cr).

input.verdict: Support: MACE puts FeVO4 on the hull (Ehull 0), so it should form at Fe:V≈1. The MEGNet HSE gap is 2.75 eV. HSE usually overestimates this; the experimental FeVO4 gap is about 2.0 eV, close to the 2.06 eV photons. Index 76 (Fe 0.456, V 0.459, Cr 0.085) is the closest low-Cr match to FeVO4.

content.text: The Fe-rich film (index 167) beat the FeVO4 film, so I'm using my last merit measurement on index 180, the most Fe-rich, lowest-V composition.

input.verdict: Weak support. The MEGNet GLLB gap for the Fe–Cr oxide is 1.1 eV (HSE earlier gave 2.0 eV), so Fe-rich Cr-alloyed oxides should absorb the 2.06 eV photons. Measured EQE rose from 0.051% at the FeVO4 composition to 0.077% at Fe 0.71. Index 180 (Fe 0.70, V 0.17) continues that trend toward Fe-rich, low-V compositions and is next to the best point so far. The GP top pick (190) is in the same area.

content.text:
I submitted index 167 (Cr 0.106, Fe 0.709, V 0.185) as the best composition. It had the highest EQE I measured, 0.077%. That's a low result: every film I measured stayed below 0.08%, and I can't tell how far it is from the library's best. With only 3 measurements I covered two areas of the library.

| Index | Cr / Fe / V | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 76 | 0.085 / 0.456 / 0.459 | 0.051 |
| **167** | **0.106 / 0.709 / 0.185** | **0.077** |
| 180 | 0.126 / 0.702 / 0.172 | 0.052 |

- **First pick (index 76):** I started near FeVO4 because the MACE model puts it on the convex hull, meaning it's stable and should form in the film. It is also a known photoanode material. It gave the lowest result.
- **Second pick (index 167):** I moved to the iron-rich corner. The band-gap model puts an Fe–Cr oxide gap around 2.0 eV, just below the 2.06 eV illumination, so it should absorb. This was the best result.
- **Third pick (index 180):** a close neighbour of 167, a bit higher in Cr and lower in V. EQE fell back to about the FeVO4 level. The peak in this corner looks narrow, or the difference is measurement noise.

I didn't check any of the five available XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are actually in these films is unconfirmed. The chromium-rich and vanadium-rich corners were never measured.
